gen-dafont-klill-fs-fira-sans: Smooth, wide-set and sturdy. Klill and Fira Sans both skip any thick-thin shift, and Fira's big x-height keeps a long page of text feeling open and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-nunito: Nunito has big round bowls and terminals that finish well clear of the stem. And Klill, with its single-nib look and widely spaced curve endings, makes the stiffer partner, so a long passage would feel softer than the heading promises.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy, first of all. Klill hums along at a constant line weight and keeps its curve endings apart, while Public Sans is the one with a hefty lowercase and broad counters built for the long haul.
gen-dafont-klill-general-sans: Clean and orderly. Klill and General Sans both ride on a steady pressure, and General's tall x-height and smooth bends mean a long passage glides along without a snag.
gen-dafont-klill-switzer: Klill's big-bodied lowercase is what you notice first. Switzer shares that build, adding wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line, and the likeness between them is the quality that holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-neco: Neco reads with dignity, its strokes swelling gently from hairline to stem. Lemon Milk, loose, wide and rounded like a rolling-ball pen trail, adds the friendliness that makes the pairing striking.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-recia: Friendly and striking, Lemon Milk spreads its rounded letters wide with no swelling at the stroke ends. And Recia, a text serif with light modulation and generous openings, supplies the sharper, more authoritative side.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-lora: Literary and bookish, Lora keeps a modest hairline thinning at its curves. Lora also gives a long passage a broad, welcoming c, while Lemon Milk stays wide-tracked and looks like neatly bent pipe cleaner.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads with a quiet thick-thin cadence and a prominent x-height, literary and universal. Shrink Lemon Milk and its wide rounded strokes lose their punch.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-fs-rowan: Minecraftia lingers, one character per beat, with towering lowercase. Rowan, a friendly serif with generous curve openings and a modest thick-thin difference, would carry a long passage in a literary, easygoing way.
